statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 20%, at the floor of the watch band and below the 25% block threshold, while Stress stays high at 70%.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at WATCH for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD alike. The 22:00 UTC Globex reopen resolved the checkpoint flagged an hour earlier in a benign way: NQ is up 0.11% inside a band about 0.18% wide on thin volume, and Micron's record fiscal Q4 did not produce upside continuation. Long-end yields near multi-decade highs, crude near $90 and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz sequencing dispute keep Stress high without establishing an observed one-way Nasdaq-100 price path. The narrowest window of raised conditional risk is the 1 October cluster between 12:00 and 15:00 UTC, covering jobless claims, the US cash open and ISM Manufacturing.
headline: Globex reopens quietly and Micron's record quarter fails to extend; Tail eases to 20% at the watch-band floor
body: NQ futures reopened after the 21:00-22:00 UTC CME halt and last printed 30,733.50, up 34.75 points or 0.11% from the 30,698.75 settle, inside a narrow 30,684.50 to 30,740.50 reopen band on roughly 2,722 contracts; Investing.com independently shows 30,736.00 against the same previous close. That is a thin, contained reopen rather than a directional leg, and it resolves the checkpoint flagged an hour earlier: Micron's record fiscal Q4 did not extend into a one-way memory-led path. Micron reported revenue of $54.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $33.42 against $31.16 expected, with fiscal Q1 2027 guidance of $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion and adjusted EPS of $38.15 plus or minus $1.00, yet the shares slipped 0.78% after hours to $1,056.75 from a $1,066.10 close as investors weighed rising capital spending. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,408.50, up 0.23%, exactly at its session low after a 30,630.45 high, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.24% to 26,861.06, the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,651.54 and the Dow dropped 0.86% to 50,906.05. September finished with the Dow down 4.9%, the S&P 500 down 0.7% and the Nasdaq up 1.7%. VIX settled at 16.34, up 1.87%, inside a 15.62 to 16.61 range, so there is no volatility stress to corroborate a pathological path. The dominant stress channel remains rates and energy: the latest H.15 column, dated 29 September, shows the 2-year at 4.89%, the 10-year at 5.26% and the 30-year at 5.59%, while 30 September reporting put the 10-year at 5.29% as yields climbed; WTI trades at $90.16, up 1.16%, and Brent at $97.63, up 1.53%. Geopolitically the Strait of Hormuz picture eased at the margin, with Kpler-based estimates of about 16.3 million barrels per day of regional crude exports in September, the highest since the war began, and the dispute over Tehran's seven-day proposal now described as one of sequencing rather than plan components, though tanker insurance costs remain elevated. Cooler August core PCE at 0.2% against a 0.3% consensus had already pared October Federal Reserve hike odds. Each of those inputs is a Stress or Confidence input; none is observed evidence of mean-reversion failure, so Tail eases one point to 20%. Shared Finviz context was not usable for this run: the published file is dated 29 September at 23:14 UTC, roughly 23 hours old, and is marked partial with its calendar and futures sections unavailable, so this assessment rests entirely on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment. Tail sat at 15-18% through the Asian and European hours of 30 September, stepped into the watch band from 12:00 UTC as the US session developed, peaked at 23% between 15:00 and 16:00 UTC and eased to 21-22% into and after the cash close. Stress held between 65% and 72% throughout, Confidence between 85% and 88%, and the dominant mode was mixed for every slot except the first three.
outlookSummary: The path eases out of the watch band for eleven slots between 23:00 UTC on 30 September and 09:00 UTC on 1 October, reaching a 17% low through the orderly mid-Asia hours, on the assumption the contained reopen range persists. Conditional Tail re-enters the watch band at 10:00 UTC and peaks at 23% across 13:00 and 14:00 UTC, where the US cash open and ISM Manufacturing stack inside two hours; those slots are scored event/whipsaw because a two-sided reaction is the base case and sustained directional continuation would be the first genuine amplifier. Tail then decays through the US afternoon, ticking up once for the 19:00 UTC power hour, and holds at the 20% watch-band floor into the CME halt with Friday's payrolls still unresolved. Stress stays between 68% and 73% throughout on long-end yields and crude, and Confidence drifts from 88% to 83% as the projection extends from the verified reopen reference levels.

forecastDetail.comment: Globex reopened at 22:00 UTC with NQ at 30,733.50, up 0.11% on a 30,684.50-30,740.50 band and roughly 2,722 contracts; Micron's record fiscal Q4 did not extend into continuation, and with VIX at 16.34 the tape stays two-sided, so Tail eases to the watch-band floor.

Mid-Asia keeps a wide conditional split between quiet equities and a multi-decade-high long end with Brent near $97.63; that cross-asset conflict is scored through Stress rather than Tail, so Tail holds in the low band.

The quietest projected slot takes conditional Tail to its horizon low on the assumption Asian ranges stay contained, consistent with the 16% published for the matching hour a day earlier and with no scheduled US release inside the hour.
